description: The zero-length literal (ISO §2023:8.3.3.1: 'If the opening and closing delimiters are contiguous, the length of the literal is zero, and it is known as a zero-length literal') in every spelling the alphanumeric, national and boolean formats admit - "", '', X"", N"", NX"", B"", BX"" (CobolLiteral.IsZeroLength). Not the same construct as ref-mod-zero-length-2023 (a reference modification of length zero). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1 'The implementor must allow for nonnumeric literals of 1 through 160 characters in length.', its general format the quoted {character-1} with at least one character-1; §2002:8.3.1.2.1.2 SR1 'shall be greater than zero and less than or equal to 160 alphanumeric character positions', and §2002:8.3.1.2.3.2 SR1 and §2002:8.3.1.2.4.2 SR1 the same 'greater than zero' for the boolean and national literal; §2014:8.3.1.2 'If the opening and closing delimiters are contiguous, the length of the literal is zero, and it is known as a zero-length literal.', §2014:8.3.1.2.1.3 GR3 'If character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal.' (§2014:8.3.1.2.3.3 GR4 and §2014:8.3.1.2.4.3 GR3 alike), and §2014:E.3 item 39 records it: 'Zero-length literals. A literal may now be of zero length.' (VCR row 7.30). GnuCOBOL 3.2 corroborates (zero-length-literals: unconformable in cobol85.conf and cobol2002.conf, ok in cobol2014.conf). Gated position-blind on the TOKEN by LiteralScreen.GateFormat (kb/Work PB895).
vcr: zero-length literals (2014 introduction, §2014:E.3 item 39); VCR row 7.30
